_what: Similitude (the triset dominoes) — commercial concepts, 2026-09-02. Posted as a deck to the similitude-commercial-design chat's Compare tab for ♥/✕. Each card is one commercial; the last cards are tagline options.

items.text: Three triangle cards land on a wood table: a comet, a mountain goat, a salt flat. A voice asks: what do these have in common? Nothing happens. A hand turns one card. Then, off screen: "they all have peaks." The middle triangle fills in and a brand-new card is drawn on the spot — the thing that unites them.

sections.label: Why it works
sections.text: The silence IS the pitch. Regular dominoes never make you wait; this one makes you think, and the payoff is a card nobody has ever seen.

items.text: Same three cards, two different tables. Table one: "jagged line running through them." Table two: "they're all cold." Both tables get a new card, and the two new cards are completely different. Split screen at the end: two decks that came from the same start and don't look alike.

sections.label: Why it works
sections.text: This is the whole difference from dominoes in one image: the game is what YOU see, so your deck ends up being a portrait of how you think.

items.text: BEFORE: a beige room, four people matching dots. "Four." "...four." A clock. AFTER: same four people, Similitude on the table, everyone talking at once — "burnt toast and a REDWOOD?" "column up the middle!" "...ok fine." A new card gets drawn while they argue.

sections.label: Why it works
sections.text: The same before/after shape as the boys ad — the joke does the selling. The dots are the villain.

items.text: One table, one evening, sped up. The deck starts as a small stack. Every set found makes a card appear, drawn in. By the end the table is tiled edge to edge in triangles and the stack is twice the size. Last frame holds on the tessellation.

sections.label: Tagline
sections.text: The deck you finish with is bigger than the one you started with.

sections.label: Why it works
sections.text: The made card is the feature no other game has. It also just looks beautiful when the triangles tile.

items.text: Slow. Macro on the cards one at a time — braided river, hot spring, frozen falls, redwood, comet — each one a small window. The camera pulls back and they're all one table. Then a hand slides two together along a shared edge and the wavy line in one continues into the other.

sections.label: Tagline
sections.text: Little slices of life. Find the seam.

sections.label: Why it works
sections.text: The art is a reason to buy on its own. This one sells the fractal/nature angle and could double as the product page video.

items.text: No product shots until the end — just the audio of a table trying to convince each other. "A candle stub and a sunflower." "One column, straight up." "That's a stretch." "Look at it!" Cut to the two cards. Oh. It IS a column. New card drawn.

sections.label: Why it works
sections.text: The social half: there are no wrong answers but you still have to convince the table. That's what makes it a game and not a puzzle.

items.text: Dominoes, but you make up the dots.

sections.label: The idea
sections.text: Dominoes tell you the match with pips. Similitude has none — the connection is yours to invent. This one names that in one line and keeps your dominoes hook.

sections.label: The idea
sections.text: Your line as given. Names the audience straight out — the person who buys it wants to be that person.

sections.label: The idea
sections.text: Doubles as a description of the cards (no words, no numbers) and of the game (you name the match). Pairs well with the name — Similitude is a word you have to think about too.

items.text: What do a comet and a canyon have in common? You tell us.

sections.label: The idea
sections.text: The game as a question. Swap the two things every time it runs — every poster is a different pair.
